problem_summary.summary: Advance a binary cell grid by one generation under the eight-neighbor Game of Life rules, applying every change simultaneously.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: an m x n grid of 0 (dead) and 1 (live). Update the board in place to its next generation; return nothing.

brute_force.explanation: Read neighbor counts from the unchanged input while writing each cell's next state into a separate grid. Copy the completed next generation back to the input afterward.
brute_force.correctness_idea: The temporary grid ensures every decision uses only the same original generation, which is required because all cells update simultaneously.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(mn) — each cell checks at most eight neighbors and is copied once.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(mn) auxiliary for the next-generation grid.

optimized.explanation: Encode each cell's next state in its existing integer: add 2 when it will be alive next generation. During the first pass, count current live neighbors with (value & 1), which reads the low bit and ignores the encoded next state. During a second pass, shift every value right by one to keep only the next state.
optimized.correctness_idea: The low bit retains each cell's original state throughout the decision pass, so updates cannot influence later neighbor counts. The added high-bit marker independently records the next state; the final shift commits all updates simultaneously.
optimized.time_complexity: O(mn) — each cell examines at most eight neighbors in the first pass and is committed once in the second.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary — the next state is encoded in the input grid; the fixed direction arrays use constant space.

steps.event: Process row 0 in the encoding pass.
steps.condition: A dead cell is marked only with 3 live neighbors; a live cell survives with 2 or 3.
steps.action: No cell in row 0 is alive next generation; values remain [0,1,0].

steps.event: Process row 1 in the encoding pass.
steps.condition: At [1,0], 3 neighbors cause birth; [1,1] is live with 5 and dies; [1,2] is live with 3 and survives.
steps.action: Encode next-live state by adding bit 2 at [1,0] and [1,2].

steps.event: Process row 2 in the encoding pass.
steps.condition: The live cell at [2,0] has 1 and dies; [2,1] has 3 and survives; [2,2] has 2 and survives.

steps.event: Process row 3 in the encoding pass.
steps.condition: Only the dead center cell [3,1] has exactly 3 live neighbors.
steps.action: Set its next-state bit, producing the encoded board.

steps.event: Commit the next generation by shifting each encoded value right once.
steps.condition: The low bit is the old state and the high bit is the computed next state.

edge_cases.case: Cell at a corner or edge
edge_cases.handling: Only in-bounds neighbors contribute to its count.
No cell reaches three live neighbors, so all remain dead.

edge_cases.case: A live cell with exactly two or three live neighbors
edge_cases.handling: Its next-state bit is set, so it remains alive after the commit pass.
Neighbor counts use only low bits from the original generation; encoded next states do not affect later decisions.
